failure_patterns.pattern: answer_format: Returned an overlong or overly descriptive form instead of the shortest answer (e.g., added a middle initial, organization type, or extra alternatives).

rejected_edits.content: - Use the shortest context-supported conventional form that satisfies the requested slot. Do not expand a sufficient name with initials or middle names merely because a source uses them. For common terms, answer at the clue’s requested category level: omit narrower subtype or function qualifiers unless they are canonical or needed to identify the requested answer.
rejected_edits.target: - Use the context-supported conventional form of a name, and include additional name parts only when needed to distinguish otherwise-confusable entities.

rejected_edits.content: - Resolve the direction of relational clues: if a prompt asks for a whole or site identified through one of its parts, return the whole or site, not the part. In an implicit attribution clue, a possessive such as “his” or “her” before a work can point to the person behind it; when the answer slot is that person, return the creator rather than the work title.
rejected_edits.target: - Before answering, parse the requested answer slot and all identifying relations or properties, then test the candidate against the complete clue. When snippets compete, prefer factual evidence that fits those details; keyword overlap in a title or heading, prominence, or a similar name alone is not enough. Do not substitute a related entity, example, remedy, or mechanism for the requested answer.
